formulas.name: Precision rectifier (super diode)
f: Op −amp removes the diode drop : output follows input
for V<sub>in</sub> > 0 even for millivolt signals
notes: Tip: Used for small-signal rectification and AC voltmeters.

formulas.name: Voltage multipliers
notes: Tip: High voltage at low current (CRT, X-ray, Cockcroft–Walton).

formulas.name: Multistage amplifier
f: n identical stages : fH(n) = fH √1n −12
notes: Where: A₁, A₂ = stage gains, f<sub>H</sub> = upper cut-off of one stage, n = number of stages
Tip: Bandwidth shrinks as stages are added.

formulas.name: Coupling methods
f: RC (audio, cheap, no DC), transformer (impedance matching,
notes: Tip: RC coupling blocks DC and has a flat mid-band.

formulas.name: Astable multivibrator (BJT)
notes: Where: R = base resistor (Ω), C = timing capacitor (F)
Tip: No stable state — square-wave generator.

formulas.name: Monostable & bistable
notes: Where: R in Ω, C in F; T = pulse width (s)
Tip: Schmitt trigger is a bistable with hysteresis.

formulas.name: 555 applications
notes: Where: R<sub>A</sub>, R<sub>B</sub> = timing resistors (Ω), C = timing capacitor (F)
Tip: Control pin (5) changes thresholds → VCO/PWM.

formulas.name: VCO (e.g. 566)
notes: Tip: Frequency is proportional to control voltage — used in PLLs and FM.

formulas.name: Schmitt trigger thresholds
notes: Where: V<sub>sat</sub> = output saturation voltage, R₁, R₂ = feedback divider (R₁ to ground)
Tip: Squares up noisy signals — no false triggering.

formulas.name: Frequency-response shortcuts
notes: Where: R<sub>eq</sub> = resistance seen by the capacitor, C<sub>c</sub> = coupling capacitor, C<sub>in</sub> = input capacitance, C<sub>f</sub> = feedback capacitance
Tip: Miller effect lowers f<sub>H</sub> in CE amplifiers.

mcqs.q: Q1. No-load output of a voltage doubler
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) 2V<sub>m</sub> Two capacitors charge to V<sub>m</sub> each and add.

mcqs.q: Q2. A Schmitt trigger is used to
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) Square up noisy signals (hysteresis) Two thresholds UTP/LTP stop chattering.

mcqs.q: Q3. Cascading identical amplifier stages makes the overall bandwidth

mcqs.ans: Ans: (d) Lock range ≥ capture range Once locked, it can follow a wider range than it can acquire.
